name: pwrite64
synopsis: ssize_t pwrite64(int fd, const void *buf, size_t count, off_t offset);
description: pwrite64 writes up to count bytes from the buffer starting at buf to the file descriptor fd at the specified offset without changing the file offset. It is the 64-bit version of pwrite, used on Linux for large file offsets.

parameters.name: buf
parameters.description: Buffer containing the data to write

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Offset from the beginning of the file

return_value.success: Returns the number of bytes written
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: Non-blocking I/O and the operation would block (from write(2))
fd is not a valid file descriptor or is not open for writing (from write(2))
fd is attached to an object not capable of seeking (from lseek(2))
Offset would cause an overflow (from lseek(2))

bugs: On Linux, if a file is opened with O_APPEND, pwrite64 appends data to the end of the file regardless of the offset, contrary to POSIX requirements.
versions: Linux 2.6 (renamed from pwrite); glibc support added in glibc 2.1
